Since we recently migrated to TypeScript 3.7 (https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4097), we can now generate declaration files for the library consumers even if the TypeScript migration is not finished yet.

It is possible thanks to the new [`--declaration` and `--allowJS` support](http://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-3-7.html#--declaration-and---allowjs).

Even with a partial migration we get some pretty good declaration files even if we still have 197 `any` on the public API (the existing JSDocs helped here). What is mainly missing is inline documentation tho, but this is still way better than what currently exists IMHO.

Since we heavily rely on JSDoc in JavaScript files the risk is to have some incorrect types declared, this is not an issue a long as it is not in the public API (we do not use `checkJS` in development).

To check the public API I used [`api-extractor`](https://api-extractor.com) to generate some report files: https://gist.github.com/yannickcr/e46632add9a98578269616613a5bad56 Let me know if you see any issue.

(**Theses files are not part of this PR**, this is just an extraction of what was generated to help to find some incorrect types.)

I only generated the report from the `index.d.ts` so we are missing the widgets and connectors. I will properly regenerate the file so we can have a better overview of the public API (this does not affect the declaration files generated in this PR).

The public API surface is waaaayyyy larger than what I thought, I think it will be difficult for us to identify incorrect types even with this flattened declarations :neutral_face: .
Exposing wrong types is worse than no types. I think we should only export the types coming from TypeScript files, and continue the TypeScript migration as best effort.
On a quick glance the types don't seem wrong, but it does seem hard to check these. I wonder if there's an option to create more files (maybe without api extractor?)
There seem to be duplicate types there though, `Hit` seems  to be there three times?

@Haroenv There is 3 files in the gist (1 for `src/index.es.ts`, 1 for `src/widgets/index.ts` and 1 for `src/connectors/index.ts`), each of them containing `Hit` (this is normal since they were generated separately).

To get multiple files you can checkout this branch and run `yarn build` and check the `.d.ts` files in the `es` directory. May be it would be clearer?

@francoischalifour It is also possible (just remove `allowJs` from `tsconfig.declaration.json`), but since we are not sure they are wrong it would be too bad IMHO to skip all JSDocs and TypeScript type-check on all JavaScript files from this assumption.

When we publish the typescript version for the first time manually, we need to make sure the version in `version.ts` is modified like `x.y.z-experimental-typescript`, so that it will have a correct user agent, but it shouldn't be committed to git.

Correct, for publishing an experimental, the flow would be:

1. `VERSION=4.X.X-typescript.X yarn build`
2. `yarn build:types`
3. ` npm publish --tag typescript`

(or `typescript-experimental`)

As decided together, we'll publish this as experimental release on the npm tag `experimental-typescript` to avoid potentially breaking users builds (stricter typecheck) while being able to let internal and external users to experiment with the generated typings.

This release will be handled manually at first (with instructions in the `CONTRIBUTING.md` file) and then will be automated with Ship.js.

Additionally to the standard release this experimental one will contains: 
* declaration files (generated with the `yarn build:types` command)
* `types` entry in `package.json`

This PR will be updated accordingly.

In a separate PR, we will add an additional type check with `tsc` and the `allowJs` + `checkJs` flags to `true`. This will allows us to see the remaining errors in the JavaScript files and fix them progressively (by updating JSDoc or migrating JS files to TS). This check will be ran by the CI and will be allowed to fail.
